sources.citation: Ciucci, Luca. 2016. Inflectional morphology in the Zamucoan languages. Asunción: CEADUC (Biblioteca Paraguaya de Antropología 103). 790 pp. [HAL preprint hal-04429404]
sources.note: §2.2 'Old Zamuco phonology and orthography' (pp. 50-51): Chomé paid little attention to phonetics/phonology; footnote 42: 'nothing is known about the accent'. Reconstructs vowels /a e i o u/ + nasality, consonant chart, CV syllable preference; no stress rule.

sources.citation: Chomé, Ignace. 1958 [ms. before 1745]. Arte de la lengua zamuca (Présentation de Suzanne Lussagnet). Journal de la Société des Américanistes 47: 121-178.
sources.note: No section or remark on 'acento' anywhere in the 58 pages (all pages' scanned downloaded from Persée and searched; Lussagnet's French introduction pp. 121-123 also silent). The only pronunciation remarks concern word-final <e> 'que no se pronuncia' vs 'que se pronuncia' (pp. 135, 162-163) and 'la A final se pronuncia con Aspiracion leve' (p. 174 area). The edition prints sporadic grave accents on some Zamuco forms (e.g. omè 'dative particle' p. 130, Enè, zannè), never explained.

sources.citation: Kelm, Heinz. 1964. Das Zamuco: eine lebende Sprache. Anthropos 59: 457-516, 770-842.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: pp. 460-465 contain phonetic observations comparing Chomé's Old Zamuco spellings with living 'Zamuco' (Ayoreo); cited by Ciucci 2016: 50 n. 43 as the basis of his Old Zamuco phonology section. Might comment on Chomé's accent marks, though Ciucci, having read it, still concludes the accent is unknown.

sources.note: Critical edition of the rediscovered Chomé dictionary manuscript with linguistic commentary; the only place a systematic account of Chomé's diacritics (grave accents, 'e que no se pronuncia') and hence any recoverable accent information for Old Zamuco would appear. Would supersede Ciucci 2016 fn. 42 if it says anything.
